title: Babu Khan v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ashok Bhushan, J.; Sunita Agarwal, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to para 6.9 complaint.
headnote: A writ challenging the correctness of an electricity bill and a citation issued on that bill is not entertainable. The consumer must file a complaint under paragraph 6.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Babu Khan petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash a citation dated 11 July 2012, which he said had been issued on a wrong electricity bill. The petition in substance challenged the correctness of that bill. After hearing counsel for the petitioner and for the respondents, a Division Bench of Ashok Bhushan and Sunita Agarwal, JJ. held that the statutory course was a complaint under paragraph 6.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and dismissed the writ.

holding_units.holding: A writ petition that challenges the correctness of an electricity bill and a citation issued on that bill cannot be entertained; the remedy is an appropriate complaint under paragraph 6.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: whether the electricity bill and the citation dated 11 July 2012 were correct
